headline: 愛丁堡藝穗節：親子與鋼管
context: 愛丁堡藝穗節（Edinburgh Fringe）持續到 8 月 31 日。給小朋友看的節目裡，有機器人幫手秀，也有像昆汀·布雷克筆下阿米塔太太那樣的古怪角色。另一頭，鋼管舞表演也悄悄攻佔了藝穗節，好幾組表演者從紐約地下文化跳到探討神經多樣性的題材都有。

sources.summary: With abs like Olympians and skin like hide, pole dancers are besieging the festival. We meet four high-flying, high-octane acts tackling everything from New York’s underbelly to neurodiversity If you tell someone in Edinburgh you’re going to see a pole dancing show, they might direct you towards the so-called Pubic Triangle, where the city’s strip clubs are. But pole dance is actually a big part of the festival this year, popping up in sweaty, dazzling shows right across the fringe. Not only do these acts show off amazing physical feats, they also tell stories that range from one woman’s HIV diagnosis, to the relationship between a neurodivergent mother and son. Since the boom of the 1990s, when Zoe Ball famously had a pole in her living room, pole has been taught at dance studios, has become a competition sport – there’s a campaign to get it into the Olympics – and made its way from cabaret stages to theatres. It’s an impressive and fiendishly difficult art. Continue reading...
sources.title: ‘We are defying the laws of physics!’ How pole dancing exploded into the Edinburgh fringe

voice_text: 愛丁堡藝穗節，今年連鋼管舞都殺進來了。藝穗節辦到八月底，給小朋友看的節目裡，有機器人幫手秀，也有像昆汀·布雷克筆下阿米塔太太那樣的古怪角色，很適合闔家觀賞。另一頭，鋼管舞表演悄悄攻佔了藝穗節現場，好幾組表演者身手不輸奧運選手，題材從紐約地下文化到神經多樣性都有人挑戰。
